newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-WORLD NUMBER FOUR LOSES BUT CHINA WIN.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-WORLD NUMBER FOUR LOSES BUT CHINA WIN.

text.p: Perennial winners China moved within striking distance of a women's team quarter-final place at the world table tennis championships on Friday.
But there was a surprising 3-2 defeat for 1995 bronze medalists Hong Hong, fielding former mainland Chinese players Chai Po Wa and Chan Tan Liu, at the hands of Germany.
Hong Kong had won their three previous round-robin matches in their six-nation group.

Germany, the only team in the Group with a 100 percent record, are set to head the standings for an automatic quarter-final place. Hong Kong can still finish second by beating North Korea on Saturday to go into the last 16.
While Chai was successful in both her visits to the table against the Germans, Chan lost twice including the decider against European champion Nicole Struse, which went the full distance.
Hong Kong had whitewashed Italy 3-0 earlier on Friday, while the Germans edged North Korea 3-2.
But no-one in Manchester is taking any bets against China winning the title for the 11th time in the last 12 championships.
After blanking Canada 3-0, the Chinese followed up with a 3-1 victory over closest group rivals Japan with world number four Yang Ying suffering a surprise defeat by 75th-ranked Rika Matsuoka.

Chinese women's team coach Lu Yuansheng accused Japan of cowardice for not fielding their best player, Chiro Koyama, formerly He Zhili who was a member of China's 1985 world championship-winning team and won the individual title two years later.
Japan claimed Koyamura, the current Asian champion, was being rested for Saturday's important match against Russia, but that didn't placate Lu.

"It showed cowardice," Lu said. "Koyama has no confidence of beating our world champion Deng Yaping again which is why she didn't play. But even if she had played China would have still won by 3-2 at least."
The men have only played two matches each over the first two days of the championships which end on May 5.
Defending champions China overpowered Italy 3-0. The Chinese, spearheaded by world champion Kong Linghui, rested Atlanta Olympic gold medalist Liu Guoliang in favour of silver medalist Wang Tao.

Sweden, who won the team title three times in succession before losing the crown two years ago, called up world number two Jan-Ove Waldner for the match against Austria after missing Thursday's opener.
The Swedes won 3-0, but 30-year-old European champion Waldner was less inspiring in his match against Qian Qianli, being taken the full distance by the former Chinese penholder-style player.
Waldner, the only man to complete the Grand slam of world champion in 1989, world cup winner in 1990 and Olympic gold medallist in 1992, edged it 21-11, 14-21, 21-18.
After twice quandering healthy leads in the decider, Waldner missed three match points on service before clinching it with a backhand smash.
